transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you to the clinic today?

I'm here because I've been feeling really down and depressed for a very long time now. It's been going on constantly for over two years—about two years and a month, actually. I just can't seem to shake this sadness.
Have you had any periods of feeling normal or symptom-free since this started, or has it been present most days without a break for the entire time?
No, I haven't really had any normal periods or breaks at all. It has been present almost every single day for the entire two years. This low, gloomy mood has just felt completely continuous.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Persistent Depressive Disorder, Major Depressive Disorder], but the patient describes a depressed mood that has been present almost every day for over two years with no symptom-free periods. That chronic, continuous course strongly supports Persistent Depressive Disorder and makes Major Depressive Disorder less likely as the primary diagnosis because MDD is typically episodic rather than continuously present for this duration.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a chronically depressed mood lasting continuously for over two years, present nearly every day without symptom-free intervals. This duration and persistent course are most consistent with Persistent Depressive Disorder rather than an episodic depressive disorder or a stress-related adjustment reaction.
